items.title: Catholic Church in Nigeria has supported me spiritually, financially – Jude Nnam
items.description: Renowned Nigerian composer, singer and music director, Dr Jude Nnam, has acknowledged the financial and spiritual support he has received from the Catholic Church in Nigeria during his ongoing medical treatment in India. Nnam, who is currently recuperating, said the Catholic Bishops Conference of Nigeria (CBCN) had been instrumental in supporting him throughout his medical journey, contrary to suggestions by some individuals that the Church had not done enough to assist him. In a message of appreciation to friends and supporters on his Facebook page, the music director said he was getting better by the day through God’s grace, prayers and support from the Church and well-wishers. Addressing concerns raised by some individuals over the need for the Catholic Church in Nigeria to assist with the financial burden of his treatment, Nnam said the Church had provided him with tremendous support. He particularly expressed gratitude to the Catholic Bishops Conference of Nigeria for taking responsibility for his situation and providing both financial and spiritual assistance since his arrival in India. Nnam also singled out the Secretary-General of the Catholic Secretariat of Nigeria, Rev. Fr. Michael Banjo, for his personal commitment and support. According to him, Banjo visited him in India on behalf of the Bishops Conference, bringing gifts and blessings from the bishops, and spent an entire week with him. He said the priest celebrated Mass for him daily throughout his stay before returning to Nigeria. The composer further acknowledged the individual contributions of Catholic bishops and dioceses, noting that they had supported him through telephone calls, messages and financial contributions. He also thanked friends and other well-wishers whose prayers and financial contributions had helped sustain him during the challenging period. “Be rest assured that the Catholic Church in Nigeria has supported me in this journey in no small measure, and I remain grateful,” he said. Nnam appealed for continued prayers for his recovery, expressing optimism that he would soon return to Nigeria and resume his musical and religious assignments. “By the grace of God, I shall be back soon to continue the work of my Father and my Healer,” he said. The post Catholic Church in Nigeria has supported me spiritually, financially – Jude Nnam appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Enseignement supérieur : 96 640 nouveaux bacheliers pour seulement 57 000 places
items.description: L’enseignement supérieur sénégalais fait face à une forte pression sur ses capacités d’accueil. Pour cette rentrée 2026-2027, avec 96 640 nouveaux bacheliers et près de 94 000 demandes d’orientation enregistrées, seulement 57 000 places sont disponibles. Le défi s’annonce considérable. Lors du Conseil interministériel consacré à la rentrée 2026-2027, le ministre de l’Enseignement supérieur, Boubacar Camara, a exposé les difficultés et les mesures envisagées pour faire face à la massification des effectifs. L’afflux de nouveaux bacheliers constitue l’un des principaux défis de la rentrée universitaire 2026-2027. Les établissements publics d’enseignement supérieur devront faire face à une demande d’orientation largement supérieure à leurs capacités d’accueil. Une situation qui remet au premier plan la problématique de la surcharge des universités, du déficit d’infrastructures pédagogiques et de l’insuffisance des moyens d’encadrement. Devant le Premier ministre Ahmadou Alhaminou Lô, lors du Conseil interministériel consacré à la rentrée, le ministre de l’Enseignement supérieur, de la Recherche et de l’Innovation, Boubacar Camara, a présenté des chiffres révélateurs. Sur les 96 640 nouveaux bacheliers attendus, 94 000 demandes d’orientation ont déjà été enregistrées. Pourtant, les capacités disponibles sont estimées à seulement 57 000 places. L’écart entre les demandes enregistrées et les capacités annoncées atteint ainsi 37 000 places. Un déficit qui illustre les difficultés auxquelles les pouvoirs publics devront apporter des réponses pour garantir aux nouveaux bacheliers la possibilité de poursuivre leurs études. Face à cette situation, Boubacar Camara a annoncé une décision gouvernementale portant sur 50 000 places destinées aux universités. A lire aussi : Direction de l’Enseignement supérieur : les priorités du Directeur général, le Pr Mamadou Sidibé Cette mesure doit contribuer à organiser l’accueil des nouveaux étudiants. Toutefois, les modalités précises de cette allocation et son articulation avec les capacités existantes restent à clarifier. La question des places disponibles renvoie directement au déficit d’infrastructures universitaires. Malgré les investissements consentis, les établissements continuent de subir une pression croissante sur leurs amphithéâtres, leurs salles de travaux dirigés et leurs équipements pédagogiques. Le ministre a particulièrement insisté sur l’accélération des chantiers universitaires. Selon lui, certains projets de construction, engagés depuis 2015 ou 2017, ne sont toujours pas achevés alors que des financements existent. Une situation qui ralentit l’extension des capacités d’accueil. Le département de l’Enseignement supérieur entend travailler avec le ministère chargé des Infrastructures pour accélérer la livraison des ouvrages. Les investissements concernent aussi bien les infrastructures pédagogiques que les équipements sociaux, notamment les résidences universitaires et les structures de restauration. L’augmentation des effectifs pose également la question de l’encadrement pédagogique. Boubacar Camara a reconnu la nécessité de renforcer les ressources humaines pour maintenir un taux d’encadrement acceptable. Le recours à des enseignants vacataires figure parmi les solutions envisagées, en attendant des mesures plus durables. À la surcharge des universités s’ajoute le problème récurrent du calendrier académique. Les grèves, les retards dans les orientations et les difficultés d’organisation ont progressivement entraîné un chevauchement des années universitaires. Cette situation complique l’accueil des nouvelles promotions puisque certains étudiants poursuivent encore leurs enseignements lorsque les nouveaux bacheliers doivent intégrer les établissements. Elle exerce également une pression sur les bourses, les logements et les finances universitaires. Pour y remédier, le ministre a annoncé un plan de transition et de régularisation du calendrier académique. Des financements sont prévus dans le cadre des contrats de performance afin de permettre aux universités de retrouver progressivement un fonctionnement normal. Par Daouda DIOUF

items.title: Tourisme : l’Algérie vise 8 millions de visiteurs en 2029 et mobilise sa diaspora
items.description: L’Algérie actionne le moteur de la croissance que représente le tourisme et compte sur sa diaspora pour le développer avec un objectif tracé d’attirer 8 millions de touristes à l’horizon 2029. Pour cela, la ministre du Tourisme et de l’artisanat, Houria Medahi et le secrétaire d'État auprès du ministre des Affaires étrangères, chargé de la communauté nationale à l'étranger, Sofiane Chaib, a présidé jeudi une réunion avec des opérateurs économiques, des investisseurs, des acteurs du secteur touristique, des porteurs de projets et des représentants de startups issus de notre communauté nationale à l'étranger. Le délégué général de l'Association des banques et établissements financiers (ABEF), le Directeur général adjoint du Groupe public Hôtellerie, tourisme et thermalisme (GHTT), le Directeur général de l'Agence nationale du foncier touristique (ANFT), ainsi qu'un représentant de la Direction générale des Domaines nationaux, une représentante de l'Agence algérienne de promotion de l'investissement (AAPI) ont assisté à la réunion. Les chefs des postes consulaires d’Algérie à Paris, Marseille, Strasbourg, Genève, Bruxelles et Metz étaient également présents, selon un communiqué du ministère. Le tourisme constitue désormais « l'un des piliers fondamentaux de la diversification économique, ainsi qu'un levier de création de richesse et d’emplois », a dit la ministre, en ajoutant que son secteur s'inscrit dans une vision stratégique « ambitieuse, visant à accueillir 8 millions de touristes à l'horizon 2029 » et à « renforcer les capacités d'hébergement touristique, en adéquation avec les atouts exceptionnels dont regorge notre pays. » Tourisme : l’Algérie appelle sa diaspora à s’impliquer Mme Meddahi a ensuite évoqué les opportunités d’investissement dans le tourisme en Algérie. Elle a cité la réalisation et le développement d'établissements hôteliers et de structures d'hébergement ; le tourisme saharien, de montagne, écologique, culturel et spirituel ; le tourisme thermal et de bien-être ; les villages touristiques et les espaces de loisirs ; ainsi que le transport touristique, les services numériques et les applications intelligentes, la valorisation des produits du terroir et de l'artisanat, avec leur intégration aux circuits et destinations touristiques. Dans la foulée, la ministre du Tourisme et de l’Artisanat a demandé aux membres de la diaspora algérienne à « s'impliquer dans cette dynamique ». Elle a précisé que cette contribution « ne se limite pas au seul investissement financier ». L’Algérie veut impliquer sa diaspora dans le « transfert d'expertises et de connaissances, le développement de méthodes de gestion modernes, la promotion de l'innovation et de la numérisation, l'établissement de partenariats avec des opérateurs internationaux, l'attraction de tour-opérateurs, ainsi que la promotion de la destination Algérie sur les marchés étrangers. » Elle veut en faire de « véritables partenaires » dans l'édification d'un tourisme algérien compétitif et qui se distingue par son excellence. L’article Tourisme : l'Algérie vise 8 millions de visiteurs en 2029 et mobilise sa diaspora est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: FM Dar calls for multilateralism, says bloc or unilateral politics will not work
items.description: Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar stressed the importance of multilateralism, saying bloc politics and unilateralism would not work. In an interview with Euronews , the foreign minister said Pakistan’s foreign policy was very clear: it was independent. “We believe in multilateralism,” FM Dar said, emphasising that even in the current environment, countries needed to work “double hard” to support it. “Bloc politics or unilateral politics will not work,” he added. Dar recalled that during Pakistan’s three-day presidency of a UN Security Council moot, the theme had been multilateralism and the peaceful settlement of disputes. He also highlighted Pakistan’s role in the ongoing conflict between the United States and Iran. “Pakistan believes that diplomacy and dialogue are the only way forward, even amid the extreme conflicts taking place in various parts of the world. “The more effort is put into dialogue and diplomacy, the more likely a solution will emerge,” he said. On mediation efforts between the US and Iran, FM Dar said Pakistan was the first country to condemn Israel’s attack on Iran on February 28. The foreign minister said he had called his Iranian counterpart the following day, urging him to exercise restraint and refrain from retaliating against the attack. However, he clarified that his message was not to target other Middle Eastern or Gulf countries, expressing regret that they were subsequently attacked. He maintained that Iranian officials had told Pakistan they were targeting only American military bases and not those countries. FM Dar also hailed the direct talks between the US and Iran, hosted by Islamabad after 47 years. The foreign minister said that even during the previous round of indirect talks between the US and Iran in Oman, it had been agreed that Pakistan must be present if direct talks were held. Dar also hailed the June 18 signing of the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding between the US and Iran, but regretted the subsequent violations. “Pakistan hasn’t given up. We are still working hard. We continue to persuade both parties to respect and honour what they signed on June 18,” he said. Dar also called for the free movement of vessels through all sea routes, stressing that this was a “must”. “Sooner or later — I hope sooner — we will achieve that objective because the world cannot afford [continued disruption],” he said. He said disruptions to energy supply chains and rising prices were creating difficulties for people across countries. However, he praised the government for providing fuel subsidies to low-income groups. The foreign minister said it was “high time” that regional peace was achieved through an agreed mechanism. “We all have to see the new security architecture,” he added. In late March, as US President Donald Trump announced a five-day pause in planned strikes on Iranian energy infrastructure, Pakistan, alongside Turkiye and Egypt, was instrumental in securing this fragile reprieve By early April, after weeks of intense negotiations, a two-week ceasefire was announced between the US and Iran, a breakthrough largely attributed to Pakistan’s sustained mediation. This led to a historic moment: the first round of direct US-Iran talks held in Islamabad on April 11-12, with Pakistan mediating. The Islamabad MoU between the US and Iran was signed on June 18, 2026, after weeks of intensive diplomacy, aiming to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and end the Middle East conflict. Pakistan’s economic potential On Pakistan’s economic potential and management, the deputy prime minister said there was a need to unlock the country’s potential, adding that the recent Pakistan Minerals Investment Forum was part of these efforts. “Our total external debt is $130 billion, while the estimated potential of our mineral resources and rare earth materials is between $6 trillion and $10 trillion.” “We have the potential and the capacity to match it. It’s a matter of time,” he said. Responding to a question about Pakistan’s relations with Afghanistan, Dar said, “[…] nobody wishes for Afghanistan to be a stable, economically viable and prosperous country more than Pakistan does.” Following last October’s major terrorist attacks , Pakistan shared what Dar described as credible evidence with international institutions, pointing to Afghanistan as the source of the attacks and alleging that they were sponsored by other countries. He added that the Afghan administration had provided no verifiable evidence that it had taken concrete action to curb terrorism. “We are on the front line. We have lost 100,000 people and Rs150 billion from our economy. “We genuinely want terrorism to be eradicated and eliminated,” he said. Relations with India On relations with India and the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT), the deputy prime minister said the matter depended on New Delhi. He said United Nations Security Council resolutions had granted the people of Jammu and Kashmir the right to self-determination through a plebiscite. However, with a “stroke of a pen” on August 5, 2019, India had amended its Constitution and divided the region into two union territories, a move he described as “certainly not acceptable”. Dar said New Delhi had wrongly blamed Islamabad for the Pahalgam attack as a pretext for the May 2025 conflict between Pakistan and India. He added that Prime Minister Shehbaz had immediately offered an independent investigation into the attack, but India had rejected the proposal. The foreign minister also criticised India’s decision to unilaterally place the IWT in abeyance. “It can’t be held in abeyance. How can you deprive 260 million people of water?” he said. “It’s a part of the livelihoods of 260 million people; it’s our agriculture and our food security.” “Weaponising water is not desirable. […] International treaties need to be respected, no matter how big or small a country is,” he added. Turning to Pakistan’s GSP+ status, Dar said the country’s current arrangement was due to expire at the end of this year. “The new GSP+ application would be invited. The conventions, which used to be 27, have been increased to 32. We’ll comply with every convention, and the new GSP+ regime will start from January 1, 2029,” he said.

items.title: High Court rules that Anlo Traditional Council lacks jurisdiction to adjudicate Atorkor chieftaincy dispute
items.description: The Denu High Court has ruled that the Anlo Traditional Council lacks jurisdiction over a chieftaincy dispute concerning the legitimate Dufia (Paramount Chief) for the Atorkor community in the Anloga District of the Volta Region. The Court, presided over by His Lordship Sylvester Nii Okai Ablor, also quashed a ruling that identified Torgbi Ackumey Geli Adjorlolo III of the Adjorlolo family as the legitimate Dufia (Paramount chief) for Atorkor. The Court directed the Kome-Shime Traditional Council to adjudicate the dispute and find a lasting solution, since the division falls within its jurisdiction. Background In May 2026, Torgbi Dosu Adaku VIII, through his lawyer, Torgbiga Wenya III (E. A. Vordoagu Esq.), sought legal redress at the Denu Court against a ruling by a judicial panel constituted by the Anlo Traditional Council. They argued that the Kome-Shime Traditional Area has the legitimate right to determine a chieftaincy status and succession case involving the Dosu Adaku Stool and Ackumey Geli Adjorlolo Stool, which fall within its jurisdiction. They further stated that Torgbi Samlafo IV, who presided over the panel, is a chief in the Avenor Traditional Area, which is outside the Anlo Traditional Council. They therefore asserted that the panel lacked “the legal competence and statutory authority” to adjudicate the case, since some members had been erroneously empanelled. Counsel for the applicants also indicated that Kome-Shime is a “separate, distinct and independent” traditional area and has been allocated traditional council status; therefore, its functional Judicial Committee has the power to adjudicate chieftaincy disputes. They asked the court to quash the ruling, arguing that the Anlo Traditional Council lacked the power to determine a dispute that arose outside its jurisdiction. The court granted the application on 18th November, 2026.

items.title: 2027: We’re not joining your opposition coalition, PDP tells Lukman
items.description: …Snubs November 30 summit, declares Wike’s Rainbow alliance its only coalition By Luminous Jannamike, Abuja The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) has rejected claims that it has joined the opposition Coalition for Democracy being promoted by former National Vice Chairman of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Salihu Lukman, declaring that it will not attend the coalition’s November 30 summit. The party said it had not entered into any alliance with the coalition, authorised anyone to represent it at the summit or agreed to be bound by any decision taken in its name. It maintained that its only recognised coalition arrangement was the Rainbow Coalition, backed by its National Leader, Nyesom Wike. The position was contained in a statement signed by the PDP National Publicity Secretary, Hon. Jungudo Haruna Mohammed, who said those being presented as the party’s representatives were expelled members with no authority to speak or act on its behalf. Jungudo said the individuals’ claims to the party’s leadership and representation had suffered defeats at the Federal High Court, Court of Appeal and Supreme Court. He added that the courts had issued orders restraining Kabiru Tanimu Turaki, SAN, and his associates from parading themselves as PDP leaders, while imposing financial penalties exceeding N100 million over alleged abuses of court processes and frivolous litigation. Questioning Lukman’s continued engagement with the individuals, Jungudo said, “It is therefore astonishing that Mr Salihu Lukman, who ought to be sufficiently informed about the legal status and recognised leadership of the PDP, would continue to engage these individuals and use them as a basis for associating the party with his so-called Toronto Coalition.” Describing the proposed arrangement as a political project built on misrepresentation, the PDP declared it ‘dead on arrival’, particularly because those being presented as its representatives lacked the authority to speak on its behalf. The party also threatened legal action against Lukman, his associates and other promoters of the Coalition for Democracy if they continued to use its name and institutional identity in their political activities. “The party will not hesitate to pursue appropriate legal action against any person or group that continues to unlawfully associate the PDP with this arrangement,” Jungudo warned. Reiterating its position, the party said the Rainbow Coalition, in line with Wike’s political direction and directives, remained its only recognised coalition arrangement. It consequently urged Nigerians, political stakeholders, members and supporters, as well as media organisations, to disregard reports linking its national headquarters at Wadata Plaza, Abuja, to the November 30 summit or any other political arrangement being promoted by Lukman and his associates. “The PDP will not allow its identity to be hijacked, its institutional authority misrepresented or its political interests compromised by individuals who have no mandate to speak or act on its behalf,” Jungudo said. The party maintained that it would not be bound by any resolution or commitment purportedly made in its name by the promoters of the coalition. items.title: Santé : décès du Dr Abdou Cissé, directeur de l’hôpital d’Ourossogui
items.description: Le directeur de l’hôpital d’Ourossogui, dans la région de Matam, le docteur Abdou Cissé, a succombé à ses blessures le vendredi 20 novembre 2026, à la suite d’un accident de la circulation du mois d'octobre dernier à Ndioum. L’annonce a été faite samedi, par le ministre de la Santé et de l’Hygiène publique. « Le ministère de la Santé et de l'Hygiène publique a la profonde tristesse d'annoncer le rappel à Dieu du Dr Abdou CISSÉ, survenu le 20 novembre 2026, des suites de l'accident de la circulation du mois d'octobre dernier à Ndioum », informe la tutelle à travers un communiqué publié samedi. D’après la tutelle, l’accident est survenu lors du retour du Dr Cissé, de la cérémonie de lancement d’Octobre Rose à Ndioum. Il convient de relever selon la tutelle que le Dr Abdou Cissé a consacré sa carrière au service public hospitalier avec engagement et dévouement. Au cours de son parcours professionnel, il a occupé plusieurs postes de responsabilité au sein du système hospitalier sénégalais. A lire aussi : Bassirou Sarr (ministre chargé du Budget) : « La prévention n’est donc pas une dépense accessoire » Il a notamment exercé les fonctions de chef du service administratif et financier (SAF) au Centre national d’appareillage orthopédique (CNAO), à l’hôpital pour enfants de Diamniadio, puis au centre hospitalier national Matlaboul Fawzaini de Touba, de janvier 2020 à janvier 2024, avant de prendre la direction de l’hôpital d’Ourossogui. « À travers ces différentes responsabilités, il a consacré sa carrière au service des établissements publics de santé, faisant preuve d’engagement, de professionnalisme et de dévouement. Sa disparition constitue une perte douloureuse pour le ministère de la Santé et de l’Hygiène publique et pour l’ensemble de la communauté hospitalière sénégalaise », témoigne le ministère. items.title: Université Norbert Zongo : Sawadogo T. Roger décroche son doctorat avec la mention Très honorable
items.description: L'Université Norbert Zongo de Koudougou compte un nouveau docteur en économie appliquée. Sawadogo T. Roger a soutenu sa thèse de doctorat ce vendredi 20 novembre 2026 à Koudougou. Intitulée « Essais sur le financement bancaire des économies de l'Union économique et monétaire ouest-africaine (UEMOA) », sa recherche a été validée par le jury avec la mention très honorable. Une distinction accueillie dans une ambiance de joie par ses collègues, amis et membres de sa famille. Pendant une dizaine de minutes, l'impétrant a présenté les résultats de ses travaux de recherche consacrés aux contraintes qui entravent l'accès au financement des économies de l'UEMOA. Trois principaux enseignements ressortent de son étude. D'abord, la concentration du secteur bancaire et le niveau de concurrence influencent les taux d'intérêt appliqués aux entreprises. Ensuite, les banques disposent de possibilités de refinancement auprès de la Banque centrale des États de l'Afrique de l'Ouest (BCEAO), contrairement à certaines perceptions faisant de celle-ci un facteur de limitation du financement. Enfin, la stabilité politique et sécuritaire apparaît comme un élément déterminant dans l'appréciation des risques par les banques et leur capacité à financer le secteur privé. L'impétrant a brillamment défendu son travail À l'issue de sa présentation, les membres du jury ont procédé à une analyse critique du document, formulé des observations et adressé plusieurs questions au candidat, qui a apporté des réponses satisfaisantes. Des recommandations lui ont également été faites en vue d'améliorer la qualité de son travail. Directeur de thèse du désormais docteur, le professeur titulaire Mahamadou Diarra a salué la pertinence et l'actualité du sujet, notamment au regard des difficultés de financement des économies africaines et du secteur privé. Il a également apprécié l'engagement du candidat dans le processus de recherche. Mahamadou Diarra, Directeur de thèse Selon lui, SAWADOGO T. Roger s'est montré particulièrement réceptif aux observations formulées tout au long de son parcours. Une grande partie des recommandations des trois rapporteurs ayant été prise en compte, son directeur de thèse y voit la preuve de son dévouement et de sa passion pour la recherche en sciences économiques. Visiblement heureux de cette consécration après plusieurs années de travail, le nouveau docteur a exprimé sa reconnaissance à son directeur de thèse, qui l'a accompagné et encouragé depuis ses premières années de formation, ainsi qu'à l'ensemble des professeurs ayant pris part à la délibération. Une vue des membres du jury Au terme des échanges, le jury a prononcé la validation de la thèse avec la mention très honorable. Une annonce qui a déclenché des cris de joie dans la salle, consacrant ainsi une nouvelle étape dans le parcours académique de SAWADOGO T. Roger, désormais docteur en économie appliquée de l'Université Norbert Zongo. Pr CHABOSSOU Augustin Foster C., Président du jury, Professeur titulaire en économie du développement à l’Université d’Abomey-Calavi (Bénin).Pr DIARRA Mahamadou : Directeur de thèse, Professeur titulaire en politique économique à l’Université Norbert-Zongo du Burkina Faso. Dr METOIOLE SOMÉ Dommbévin Juste, Rapporteur, Maître de conférences agrégé en sciences économiques à l’Université Norbert-Zongo. Dr KINDA Mohamed Tidjane , Rapporteur, Maître de conférences agrégé en économie du développement à l’Université Joseph-Ki-Zerbo. Dr DIANDA Issa , Examinateur, Maître de conférences agrégé en économie du développement à l’Université Nazi-Boni. Ces cinq universitaires ont constitué le jury chargé d'évaluer les travaux de recherche du doctorant sur le financement bancaire des économies de l'UEMOA. Minute.bf

items.title: Sous-marins : Scorpène ou Dolphin AIP pour la Marine royale ?
items.description: Selon plusieurs rapports internationaux, le Scorpène de Naval Group fait face au Dolphin AIP et au Type 209/1400 de TKMS pour équiper la Marine royale. Rien d’officiel pour l’heure, et la compétition reste ouverte. Un récent rapport de la plateforme spécialisée dans les questions de défense « Meta Defense » révèle l’intensification de la concurrence entre le groupe français « Naval Group » et l’allemand « TKMS » (ThyssenKrupp Marine Systems) pour vendre des sous-marins aux Forces navales marocaines. Le même rapport relève que, malgré l’avancée des négociations sur les sous-marins « Scorpène » fabriqués par la société française, ceux-ci n’ont pas encore définitivement pris le dessus sur leur concurrent allemand. Le document souligne qu’avec l’éventuelle arrivée de nouveaux concurrents d’Asie et d’Europe, les différents modèles de coopération industrielle proposés par les deux sociétés apparaissent comme un facteur décisif pour remporter les marchés. La même source insiste sur le fait que la construction locale et l’installation de pôles de coopération industrielle sont devenues un avantage concurrentiel pour décrocher les contrats militaires. Le document précise que cinq pays ont soumis des offres au Maroc pour lui fournir des sous-marins, dont la France, l’Allemagne et la Russie, qui ont proposé des sous-marins neufs à l’armée marocaine, tandis que la Grèce et le Portugal ont proposé des sous-marins d’occasion. Le rapport indique que la compétition se resserre désormais entre le sous-marin HDW Dolphin AIP et les sous-marins allemands Type 209/1400, toujours en service dans de nombreuses marines d’Europe, d’Amérique du Sud, d’Afrique et d’Asie. Dans le même contexte, un rapport de la commission des Affaires étrangères de l’Assemblée nationale française note que les négociations entre le Maroc et « Naval Group » pour l’acquisition de sous-marins de type « Scorpène » ont atteint un stade avancé. Il considère que ce projet vise à combler des lacunes dans les capacités stratégiques et à doter la Marine royale de capacités de dissuasion et de surveillance renforcées. Sur le plan technique, le sous-marin allemand Type 209/1400 allie une grande discrétion, grâce à sa faible signature acoustique, à la capacité de rester longtemps en plongée. Il atteint une vitesse d’environ 40 kilomètres par heure et dispose d’équipements avancés pour mener diverses missions. Ce sous-marin renforce sa supériorité opérationnelle par un système intégré de reconnaissance et de renseignement, comprenant notamment le système d’imagerie thermique de troisième génération « Carl Zeiss », ainsi que des systèmes d’interception des signaux radar et des communications radio. Il dispose également d’un ensemble complet d’armements incluant les missiles antinavires « Sea Spider » et « Harpoon Block 2 ». En face, les sous-marins d’attaque français « Scorpène » se distinguent par leur conception compacte, avec une longueur d’environ 66 mètres et un déplacement avoisinant 1 700 tonnes. Leur armement comprend des torpilles lourdes et des missiles antinavires « Exocet SM39 », en plus de systèmes de détection intégrés leur permettant de capter les sons émis par les sous-marins et navires ennemis et de les localiser avec précision. Ce sous-marin, exploité par certains pays comme l’Inde et le Brésil, dispose aussi d’un radar de navigation « Sagem » et d’équipements de guerre électronique. Il peut opérer environ 50 jours consécutifs, à une vitesse pouvant atteindre environ 32 kilomètres par heure en plongée. The post Sous-marins : Scorpène ou Dolphin AIP pour la Marine royale ? appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: UGEL cannot hide behind UG’s autonomy to evade Rent Commissioner – Appiagyei-Atua
items.description: Professor at the University of Ghana School of Law, Kwadwo Appiagyei-Atua, has challenged the University of Ghana Enterprise Limited (UGEL) to submit its accommodation charges to legal scrutiny. He argued that the company cannot rely on the university’s institutional autonomy to evade the authority of the Rent Commissioner. He maintains that UGEL is a legally distinct private entity, separate from the University of Ghana, and therefore cannot invoke the university’s academic freedom as grounds for resisting the Rent Commissioner’s jurisdiction over its rental premises. “Institutional autonomy cannot protect UGEL because it is a private entity, registered as being distinct and separate from UG,” he stated. Prof. Appiagyei-Atua argued that institutional autonomy, which is closely associated with academic freedom, cannot be used as a blanket protection for the company, particularly when its operations involve the provision of accommodation to students. He also raised concerns about a potential conflict of interest arising from the university’s Pro Vice-Chancellor serving as chairperson of the UGEL board. According to him, the arrangement raises questions about the university’s responsibility to protect students’ welfare while overseeing a company whose accommodation charges have become the subject of protests. The law professor contended that excessive accommodation charges undermine students’ academic freedom by creating conditions that make it difficult for them to access and fully participate in university education. He cited reports of students sleeping in classrooms and chapels or travelling long distances to attend lectures because of accommodation difficulties. “Charging cut-throat rates that force students to sleep in classrooms, chapels and travel long distances to school violates their academic freedom,” he said. He stressed that academic freedom should not be understood narrowly as a privilege enjoyed only by university management but must also protect students whose ability to pursue their education could be affected by unaffordable accommodation. He added that even if UGEL were considered part of the university, institutional autonomy could not justify actions that undermine the rights of members of the academic community. Appiagyei-Atua backs student protests Prof. Appiagyei-Atua also criticised the University of Ghana’s handling of the students’ campaign, accusing the institution of compromising its autonomy by allowing national security personnel to become involved in the matter without an invitation. He further alleged that the university had taken steps to intimidate the Graduate Students’ Association of Ghana (GRASAG), the Students’ Representative Council (SRC) and students seeking to demonstrate against the accommodation situation. He observed that GRASAG and the SRC had initially become reluctant to sustain the campaign, while concerned students continued their civil disobedience actions. Their persistence, he said, had helped bring the two student bodies back into the campaign, with the National Union of Ghana Students (NUGS) also joining the broader call. The professor urged the student leadership to remain united and sustain pressure on the university and UGEL, insisting that their demands were legitimate and reflected the interests of the wider academic community. UTAG urged to defend students’ rights Prof. Appiagyei-Atua also called on the University Teachers Association of Ghana (UTAG) to move beyond its traditional focus on the welfare and interests of lecturers and take a more active role in defending students’ rights. He argued that lecturers had a responsibility to speak up for vulnerable members of the university community, particularly students whose concerns might otherwise go unheard. “It’s time it turned away from its inward-looking approach informed by its welfarist, unionist approach to becoming human rights defenders, a voice for the voiceless on campus and in the larger society,” he said. He emphasised that students constitute approximately 80 per cent of the university’s academic community and should therefore be central to decisions affecting the institution. “Without you there’ll be no university and all lecturers will be made redundant,” he added. Prof. Appiagyei-Atua urged students and their representative bodies to remain resolute in pursuing their demands, stressing that accommodation arrangements at the university must respect students’ rights and comply with the legal protections governing rental properties.

items.title: I will deploy 2,000 ‘yellow yellow’ task force officers to check rent abuses in 2027 – Rent Commissioner
items.description: Acting Rent Commissioner Frederick Opoku says the Rent Control Department plans to deploy 2,000 task force officers across the country in the first quarter of 2027 to enforce provisions of the Rent Act. The move is expected to address widespread practices involving landlords demanding one, two or more years of rent in advance, despite the statutory restrictions on advance rent payments. Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile on Saturday, November 21, he indicated that the planned task force, which he informally referred to as the “yellow-yellow” team, would visit households and investigate landlords suspected of violating the Rent Act. “Next year, I want to deploy 2,000 task force, yellow-yellow, that I call them, to go to the households and to begin to ask questions: You are in breach of Section 25(5) of the Act. Come and explain to rent control why you should not be prosecuted,” he said. His comments follow questions about the department’s progress in enforcing the Rent Act, particularly provisions requiring landlords to seek the appropriate approval before increasing rent and restricting advance rent payments. Mr Opoku said the department was currently prioritising public education and engagement with landlords and hostel operators ahead of a nationwide enforcement exercise. He disclosed that he had engaged hostel operators in Accra on July 5, 2026, through both physical and online meetings to explain the legal requirements governing rent increases and accommodation charges. He said he had also organised a separate engagement with landlords in November to educate them on their obligations under the law. Mr Opoku explained that the department had adopted a gradual approach because of the numerous challenges confronting the rental sector and the need to address them systematically. “I have not enforced anything, but I have to do. I cannot do all at a time,” he said. Mr Opoku, however, said the department intends to move beyond education to enforcement in the first three months of 2027.

items.title: Rent Control registers 3,000 landlords in Greater Accra in three months – Commissioner
items.description: The Acting Rent Control Commissioner, Frederick Opoku, says the Rent Control Department has registered about 3,000 landlords in the Greater Accra Region within the last three months as part of efforts to formalise Ghana’s rental sector and strengthen regulation. He disclosed that the registrations were carried out through a pilot exercise at the department’s Greater Accra office, forming part of internal reforms aimed at improving landlord identification, accountability and service delivery. Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile on Saturday, November 21, Mr Opoku said the exercise was intended to address longstanding gaps in the department’s operations and ensure that landlords and tenants complied with existing legal requirements. “When I started the pilot registering, I have registered about 3,000 landlords in only Greater Accra office in the last three months,” he said. He explained that the registration drive was part of measures to ensure the department had reliable records of landlords and could verify their status when they sought assistance or lodged complaints. Mr Opoku said the department had also introduced stricter requirements for handling complaints, directing that landlords must first register with Rent Control before their grievances could be entertained. Tenants, he added, would be required to produce their rent cards as proof of their tenancy. According to him, some provisions of the law governing rental arrangements had not been enforced over the years, creating gaps in the system that his administration was seeking to address. The registration exercise forms part of broader reforms at the department, including plans to digitise its operations within the first three months of 2027. Under the proposed digital system, landlords and tenants will be able to access and download tenancy agreements online and complete them through a coded verification process. Mr Opoku said the reforms were intended to improve the department’s efficiency and ensure that Ghanaians received professional services.

items.title: Deux narcotrafiquants marocains abattus par les Garde-frontières algériens
items.description: Deux narcotrafiquants marocains ont été abattus par les Garde-frontières algériens à la frontière avec le Maroc vendredi 20 novembre, a annoncé ce samedi le ministère de la Défense nationale. « Dans la dynamique des efforts consentis visant la sécurisation des frontières nationales et la lutte contre les barons de la contrebande et la criminalité organisée, un détachement des Garde-Frontières a neutralisé hier, vendredi 20 novembre 2026, près de la bande frontalière ouest, dans le Secteur Militaire de Naama en 2ème Région Militaire, deux narcotrafiquants de nationalité marocaine, qui ont refusé d’obtempérer, alors qu’ils tentaient d’introduire sur le territoire national une quantité de kif traité s’élevant à plus de 50 kilogrammes », a indiqué le MDN dans un communiqué. Un narcotrafiquant identifié L’identité de l’un des narcotrafiquants a été établie : il s’agit du « dénommé Khelifi Laid, né à Oulad Sidi Abdelhakem, Jerada (Maroc), selon la pièce d’identité trouvée en sa possession », a précisé la même source. Cette opération réaffirme la « vigilance constante » et la « détermination » des unités de l’Armée nationale populaire déployées à travers l’ensemble du territoire national pour « faire face à ces criminels, quel qu’en soit le prix, et à mettre en échec leurs viles tentatives visant à porter atteinte à l’intégrité de notre territoire national ainsi qu’à la sécurité et à la quiétude de ses citoyens », a ajouté le MDN. items.title: 10th anniversary: Oba Ewuare II’s reign strengthens traditional institution — Sultan
items.description: The Sultan of Sokoto, Alhaji Muhammad Sa’ad Abubakar, has congratulated the Oba of Benin, Oba Ewuare II, on his 10th coronation anniversary, commending his leadership and commitment to cultural preservation, peacebuilding and national unity. The Sultan described the anniversary as a significant milestone marking a decade of traditional leadership and dedication to the progress and well-being of the Benin Kingdom and its people. In a statement issued on Saturday by Prince Bashir Adefaka, for the Sultan’s Media Team, Abubakar praised the monarch for upholding the cultural heritage, traditions and historical identity of the Benin Kingdom. He also commended Oba Ewuare II for promoting peaceful coexistence, mutual respect and unity among Nigerians across ethnic, religious and cultural divides. The Sultan noted that traditional institutions remained indispensable to national cohesion, the promotion of moral values, community development and peaceful coexistence, particularly at a time when Nigeria needed the collective wisdom and leadership of traditional rulers to address its challenges. He said the Oba’s 10-year reign had reinforced the importance of traditional institutions as custodians of history, culture, values and the aspirations of their people. According to him, the Benin monarch has also continued to serve as a rallying point for unity, stability and development. Abubakar, who is physically present in Benin City for the anniversary celebration, expressed delight at being part of the historic occasion. He said his presence demonstrated the enduring bonds of brotherhood, friendship and mutual respect among traditional rulers in Nigeria, irrespective of ethnic and regional differences. The Sultan prayed for continued good health, wisdom, strength and long life for Oba Ewuare II, urging divine guidance for the monarch as he leads the Benin Kingdom towards greater peace, prosperity and development. He also prayed for sustained peace and progress in the Benin Kingdom, Edo State and Nigeria. items.title: HURIWA mourns Vanguard Online Editor, Femi Ajasa
items.description: The Human Rights Writers Association of Nigeria (HURIWA) has mourned the death of Vanguard Online Editor, Olufemi Finayon Ajasa, describing his passing at the age of 44 as a major loss to the journalism profession and Nigeria’s media industry. Ajasa reportedly died following a brief illness. In a condolence statement issued on Thursday, November 19, 2026, HURIWA’s National Coordinator, Comrade Emmanuel Nnadozie Onwubiko, said the journalist died at a time when his experience, creativity and digital expertise were still needed in the media industry. The association described his death as particularly painful, noting that he belonged to a generation of journalists who successfully combined traditional journalistic values with the demands of digital journalism, online storytelling and editorial management. HURIWA said Ajasa’s professional career began in photojournalism at National Mirror before he moved into editorial and digital leadership roles at Vanguard, TheNewsGuru and Pulse. It described his career progression as a reflection of his dedication, versatility and commitment to the development of Nigerian journalism. The association noted that his return to Vanguard in 2022 as Online Editor demonstrated the confidence reposed in his professional competence, experience and ability to contribute to newsroom development. HURIWA extended its condolences to the management and staff of Vanguard Media Limited, the Ajasa family, friends, colleagues and professional associates, urging them to draw strength from the positive impact he made during his lifetime. The association also drew attention to the pressures and emotional demands of journalism, noting that media professionals often work under intense deadlines and challenging circumstances to keep the public informed. While acknowledging that words might not adequately ease the pain of his loss, HURIWA urged the bereaved family to take solace in the legacy Ajasa left behind and the lives he touched through his professional and personal relationships. The association prayed for the peaceful repose of his soul and asked God to grant his family, Vanguard management and the journalism community the strength to bear the loss. items.title: COP31: AbibiNsroma Foundation urges governments to turn climate pledges into action
items.description: The AbibiNsroma Foundation has called on governments and climate finance institutions to ensure that commitments made at COP31 translate into tangible support for communities vulnerable to the effects of climate change. In a closing statement as the UN climate conference ended, the foundation said adaptation finance must move beyond negotiation rooms and reach farmers, women, young people and coastal communities bearing the impact of climate change. The foundation said it attended COP31 with a call to amplify the voices of local communities and ensure the implementation of adaptation finance. It welcomed opportunities for local voices to be heard, partnerships established and renewed commitments on adaptation, loss and damage, and climate justice. However, it said communities continued to face challenges including floods, droughts, crop failures, water scarcity and loss of livelihoods, stressing that promises made at the conference must be followed by concrete action. “Promises made at COP31 must not die at COP31. Adaptation finance must move from conference halls to farms, villages, and coastal communities,” the statement said. Looking ahead to COP32, the foundation called for a shift from negotiations to implementation, urging that commitments on adaptation finance be tracked, funded and delivered. It also called for direct access to climate finance for local communities, with women, young people, farmers and indigenous communities placed at the centre of funding decisions and programme design. The foundation further stressed the need for accountability, saying it would continue to hold governments and climate funds responsible for delivering on their commitments. It said it would also strengthen community leadership by building local capacity, documenting community experiences and presenting evidence from affected communities at COP32. “COP31 will end today, but our mission continues. We leave COP31 more united, more informed, and more committed than ever,” the statement said. The foundation expressed hope that COP32 would produce measurable progress on the ground rather than a repetition of commitments made at previous climate conferences. It reaffirmed its commitment to advocacy and community engagement under the call: “From COP31 to COP32: From Pledges to Action. Time to Implement Adaptation Finance!”

items.title: Canada : une «gifle» du Pentagone à Ottawa, sur fond de menaces d’annexion de Trump
items.description: Les relations militaires entre les etats-Unis et le Canada subissent un nouveau coup de frein. Pete Hegseth, secretaire a la Guerre des etats-Unis, a fait circuler la semaine derniere une directive classifiee reduisant certains echanges bilateraux, selon plusieurs responsables cites par le Washington Post le 20 novembre. Le journal n'a pas consulte cette note et l'etendue des restrictions reste inconnue. L'un des responsables americains interroges estime qu'Ottawa recevra la decision comme une gifle. Invite a l'expliquer, Sean Parnell, porte-parole du Pentagone, declare : « Le Pentagone prend des mesures pour garantir que ses engagements avec le Canada fassent progresser des objectifs concrets de defense americains et soutiennent a terme une relation de defense redynamisee. » Le ministere americain affirme que le renseignement militaire ainsi que la cooperation au sein de l'Organisation du traite de l'Atlantique nord (OTAN) et du Commandement de la defense aerospatiale de l'Amerique du Nord (NORAD) ne seront pas concernes. Il n'a cependant pas detaille les autres relations militaires visees par la directive. Du « 51e etat » aux restrictions militaires Depuis son retour a la Maison Blanche, Donald Trump a multiplie les appels a faire du Canada le 51e etat americain . Face a Mark Carney, dans le Bureau ovale en mai 2025, il vantait encore les avantages d'un rattachement. Le Premier ministre canadien avait oppose un refus sans detour : « Ce n'est pas a vendre. Et ca ne le sera jamais. » Les droits de douane imposes par Washington et les ripostes canadiennes ont aggrave ce bras de fer. En mai dernier, les etats-Unis ont aussi suspendu leur participation a la Commission permanente mixte de defense, creee en 1940. Le Pentagone accusait Ottawa de ne pas investir assez dans son armee, bien que Mark Carney ait annonce en mars atteindre le seuil de 2 % du produit interieur brut. Pete Hegseth n'a pas limite ses attaques aux decisions officielles. En août, il a relaye une image moqueuse d'une cadette canadienne et de son instructeur, provoquant la colere du ministre canadien de la Defense. Il a aussi minimise la contribution des allies en Afghanistan, ou 158 soldats canadiens ont perdu la vie. Devant la multiplication des menaces, Ottawa a meme examine l'hypothese d'une intervention militaire americaine . Le 20 novembre, Donald Trump a encore reproche aux Canadiens de prendre trop d'assurance face a Washington : « Pour une quelconque raison, ils se sentent pousser des ailes. Eh bien, nous ne pouvons plus les laisser se sentir ainsi. » Le meme jour, les revelations du Washington Post ont ajoute une nouvelle mesure de pression militaire a ce conflit.

items.title: Rent Control to go digital by first quarter of 2027 – Rent Commissioner
items.description: The Acting Rent Control Commissioner, Frederick Opoku, has announced plans to digitise the operations of the Rent Control Department within the first three months of 2027 as part of reforms to improve service delivery and strengthen regulation of Ghana’s rental sector. He said the reforms would allow landlords and tenants to access and complete tenancy agreements online, while introducing stricter registration requirements to help the department verify the identities and status of people seeking its services. Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile on Saturday, November 21, Mr Opoku said the digital system would enable prospective tenants and landlords to download tenancy agreement forms online and complete them using a coded verification mechanism. He explained that the initiative formed part of broader internal reforms aimed at addressing longstanding gaps in the department’s operations and ensuring that its services were more professional and accessible to the public. His announcement comes amid growing public concerns over accommodation charges at the University of Ghana following a proposed 26 per cent increase in hostel fees by the University of Ghana Enterprises Limited (UGEL). The proposed increase was subsequently reduced after consultations with student leaders, triggering wider discussions about rent regulation, accommodation affordability and the protection of tenants’ rights. Mr Opoku said the department was also tightening its procedures for handling complaints by requiring landlords and tenants to provide evidence of their status before their cases could be considered. He disclosed that landlords who visit the department would first be required to register officially to establish that they are legitimate property owners or landlords before their complaints are entertained. Similarly, tenants would be required to present their rent cards as proof of their tenancy arrangements. According to him, the requirements are based on provisions in the existing law which, he said, had not been consistently enforced over the years. He argued that the failure to implement some of these legal requirements had created gaps in the rental regulation system, making it necessary to introduce internal administrative changes. “As part of my reforms, Rent Control should go digital by the first three months of next year. People will have the opportunity to go online, download the tenancy agreement, then fill it with a coded something,” he said. Mr Opoku added that the department had put measures in place during his first year in office to address operational challenges and improve the quality of services delivered to the public. He said he expected the reforms to result in more professional and efficient services, in line with the vision of the President. 3,000 landlords registered in Greater Accra As part of efforts to formalise the rental sector, Mr Opoku revealed that the department had registered approximately 3,000 landlords through a pilot registration exercise at its Greater Accra office over the past three months. He described the exercise as part of the measures being implemented to improve the department’s records and strengthen its engagement with landlords. The registration initiative, alongside the proposed digital tenancy agreement system, is expected to form part of the department’s broader efforts to improve accountability and close gaps in rental administration. Mr Opoku said the reforms were intended to ensure that landlords and tenants complied with existing legal requirements while enabling the department to provide more effective services.

items.title: I initiated Gold Fields support for you – Sports Minister says as he praises Black Challenge for reaching Amputee World Cup final
items.description: The Minister of Sports and Recreation, Kofi Adam, has praised the Black Challenge following their qualification to the final of the 2026 Amputee Football World Cup. The Black Challenge advanced into the final after beating defending champions Turkey on penalties in the semifinals in the early hours of Saturday. Prior to the game, issues of per diems owed the team were discussed with the team calling on the government to settle all of their arrears. Gold Fields stepped in to make payment to the team ahead of the semifinals, serving as motivation for the huge encounter. Amidst all the chaos, the team overcame all challenges to beat the defending champions to make the last two, a progress the minister has commended with admiration. “When I first sat down with you, the players of the Black Challenge, I told you why I had initiated discussions with Gold Fields Ghana in February 2026. I understood what you wanted to achieve in Mexico and wanted you to have the support to give it your best. At your squad unveiling, I assured you that I would work with the GFA to get the sponsorship funds released promptly,” he wrote on his social media account. “In the NPC’s 13 August submission to the Ministry, NPC Ghana proposed that the team’s World Cup expenses be covered by the Gold Fields sponsorship. Last night, NPC Ghana confirmed an agreement for each member of the delegation to receive US$8,000 in Gold Fields funding to cover approved per diems and match bonuses. “I’ve followed your progress in Mexico and watched you fight for every win. When we met, I told you that you had conquered Africa and were ready to challenge the world. You’ve done exactly that. Today, Ghana is proud of you. “My sincere thanks to Gold Fields Ghana, the GFA and NPC Ghana for supporting the team. I encourage more Ghanaian businesses to back athletes and federations across all our sports. “Congratulations, Black Challenge. You’ve earned every bit of this moment.” The Black Challenge will come up against Morocco in an all-African final to compete for the coveted trophy.

items.title: AI, fake news threaten Nigeria’s security – Ex-police PRO
items.description: DCP Olumuyiwa Adejobi, a former Nigeria Police Force Public Relations Officer (FPRO), has warned that the misuse of social media and Artificial Intelligence (AI) to spread fake news threatens national security. He gave the warning in a statement titled “The Palongo Dance of Social Media Palava”, issued on Saturday in Lagos, urging Nigerians to communicate responsibly and exercise vigilance on digital platforms. Adejobi, currently the Deputy Commissioner of Police in charge of Operations at the Delta State Police Command, described social media misuse as a growing threat to public order, national cohesion and security. “Fabricated content can provoke hostility, incite violence, create panic and undermine public confidence in institutions,” he said. The former FPRO expressed concern over the growing use of AI to generate fake images, videos, audio recordings and narratives capable of misleading the public. According to him, the technology can make individuals appear to have said or done things they never did, with serious implications for public safety and national security. Adejobi also blamed the monetisation of social media for encouraging some content creators to prioritise views, engagements and financial rewards over truth and responsibility. “Some influencers resorted to sensational headlines, unverified allegations and provocative publications without considering their consequences for individuals, institutions and the country. “Freedom of expression must be exercised responsibly and should not be used to fabricate information, destroy reputations, incite violence or deliberately mislead the public, ” he said. He urged Nigerians to verify information before believing, sharing or reposting it, describing verification as a civic responsibility in the digital age. The former spokesperson commended the Inspector-General of Police, Mr Olatunji Disu, for recently urging the public to remain vigilant against fake news and irresponsible information dissemination. He also acknowledged the efforts of former Minister of Information and National Orientation, Mr Lai Mohammed, and the incumbent minister, Mr Mohammed Idris, in highlighting the dangers of misinformation and disinformation. Adejobi called for sustained public enlightenment, strategic communication, institutional collaboration and appropriate regulatory measures to address the menace. He, however, stressed the need to balance regulation with the protection of constitutionally guaranteed freedoms, noting that legitimate criticism and dissent must be distinguished from deliberate fabrication, impersonation and incitement. The former image maker advocated a whole-of-society approach involving government institutions, security agencies, media organisations, technology companies, professional bodies, traditional and religious leaders, civil society groups and citizens. Adejobi, who said he had personally experienced the consequences of misinformation and social media manipulation, said that false narratives could cause emotional and reputational damage that might take years to correct. He warned that fabricated stories could be created within seconds, while the damage they caused could persist for years. Adejobi urged Nigerians to promote digital literacy, ethical journalism, responsible content creation, fact-checking and constructive public engagement. He said social media should serve as a platform for enlightenment, innovation, accountability, economic advancement and national development, rather than hatred, hostility and destruction. Adejobi appealed to Nigerians not to “dance Palongo,” a Yoruba expression he said his grandmother used to describe an irregular and disorderly dance, urging citizens to reject digital recklessness and embrace truth, responsibility, civility and patriotism. “Protect the country’s collective destiny from misinformation and manipulation, Nigeria is bigger than our individual interests, political affiliations, personal grievances and social media engagements,” he said. (NAN) The post AI, fake news threaten Nigeria’s security – Ex-police PRO appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Universities charging students for accommodation must comply with rent laws – Abraham Amaliba
items.description: The Director-General of the National Road Safety Authority (NRSA), Abraham Amaliba, says universities that charge students for accommodation should be subject to rent regulation, arguing that the payment of fees creates a landlord-tenant relationship. He believes the Rent Commissioner, Frederick Opoku, is justified in intervening in the ongoing dispute over university hostel charges, describing his approach as a necessary disruption to longstanding practices in the accommodation sector. Speaking on JoyNews Newsfile on Saturday, November 21, Mr Amaliba argued that the nature of the relationship should be determined by the payment made by students for occupying rooms, rather than whether they have full control over the facilities. “At the heart of the landlord-tenant relationship is the payment of rent. Now, do the universities take money from the students or not? If they take, for me, it’s rent. All other things are inconsequential, whether you have absolute control over the room or not. And that’s why you are not a tenant in your father’s house because you don’t pay rent. So once money changes from the one who lives in the room to the one who is in charge of the room, that’s tenancy, and it must be so,” he said. Mr Amaliba also called for a comprehensive regulatory framework for university and private student accommodation facilities, warning that the growing number of private hostel operators could expose students to unfair charges. He described students as particularly vulnerable economically because many depend on their parents or guardians to finance their education and accommodation. According to him, any regulation of the sector must consider students’ ability to pay while ensuring that accommodation providers operate within an appropriate framework. Mr Amaliba further challenged arguments that hostel operators should be allowed to transfer the full cost of loans and investments to students through increased accommodation charges. “I don’t like that idea, blanket statement, that, oh, went for a loan. So if you went for a loan, you should just dump everything on these vulnerable students,” he said. He argued that investors and hostel operators must consider the financial capacity of their target market, insisting that students cannot be expected to shoulder every cost associated with providing accommodation. “Your clients are not mining companies. Your clients are not bank officials. They are students,” he stressed. Mr Amaliba said the central issue should be finding a balance between allowing accommodation providers to recover their investments and protecting students from unaffordable charges. His comments come amid the disagreement between the University of Ghana Enterprises Limited (UGEL) and Rent Commissioner Frederick Opoku over hostel fees, which has triggered concerns about the cost of student accommodation.
